topic: Public context data (drought, weather and heat, precipitation, forage outlook, soils, pasture condition) for a Great Plains ranch dashboard hosted as a static GitHub Pages site, plus brief evidence for the candidate operational features

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Choose public context by when it was released, not by the week it covers. Show the latest U.S. Drought Monitor (USDM) map that was public by as_of: released Thursday 08:30 ET, valid on the Tuesday two days earlier. Label it 'valid <Tue>, released <Thu>'. as_of must carry an offset or IANA time zone.
rules.decision_supported: Whether the drought context shown beside the ranch snapshot was actually knowable at as_of, so the page does not seem to know the future
rules.required_inputs: as_of with time zone; USDM MapDate/ValidStart; official release schedule
rules.context: All locations and seasons; any weekly public product (USDM, NASS Crop Progress)
rules.evidence: OBSERVED: the USDM home page states 'The data cutoff for Drought Monitor maps is each Tuesday at 8 a.m. EDT' and maps 'are released each Thursday at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time'. It showed map released Oct 15 2026, data valid Oct 13 2026. The county data service for Hughes Co. SD returned rows such as '20260929,...,2026-09-29,2026-10-05,1' and '20260922,...,91.73,8.27,...,2026-09-22,2026-09-28,1'. I ran node docs/audit/diagnostics/context.usdm-asof.research.mjs and it printed 'naive (ValidStart <= as_of <= ValidEnd): MapDate 20260929 (None 68.45%, D0 31.55%...) <- released 2026-10-01 08:30 ET, AFTER as_of' versus 'release-aware (released by as_of): MapDate 20260922 (None 91.73%, D0 8.27%...)' for both America/Chicago and America/Denver. The existing docs/audit/diagnostics/context.research.mjs, which I re-ran, printed 'valid date is 8.5 days old at as_of' and 'USDM valid-date age seen by a viewer ranges from 2.02 to 9.02 days'.
rules.limitations: Federal-holiday shifts are not modelled. The cutoff wording differs between official pages ('8 a.m. EDT' on USDM; '7 a.m. Eastern Time' on SD DANR and sdresponse.gov; '7 am Eastern'/'7 a.m. EST' on drought.gov). These agree only if read as 12:00 UTC. The ArcGIS layer stores MapDate/ReleaseDate as epoch values that convert to 07:30 UTC (3:30 a.m. ET on release day, before the real 08:30 release), so its times must be treated as date-only.
rules.configurable: Schedule: no, it is fixed by the publisher. Ranch time zone: yes, it must be set per ranch because SD and NE each span Central and Mountain time.
rules.missing_data_blocks: If as_of has no offset or zone (true today: meta.csv holds '2026-09-30T18:00'), the page cannot decide confidently which map was public near Thursday morning. It should show 'time zone not set' and not pick silently.
rules.recommendation: Adopt. Store released_at and valid_date for every context row, and select rows by released_at <= as_of. Add a time zone to meta.csv.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Mark the drought context stale when (as_of minus USDM valid date) is more than about 9.1 days, meaning a weekly release was missed or the fetch failed. Never read a missing or failed fetch as 'no drought'.
rules.decision_supported: Whether the drought panel can be trusted this week
rules.required_inputs: USDM valid date; as_of with time zone; fetch/retrieval timestamp
rules.evidence: Derived from the published weekly schedule. Diagnostic output: 'USDM valid-date age seen by a viewer ranges from 2.02 to 9.02 days (release lag + 7-day cycle)'. IEM and ArcGIS copies both showed the current week (IEM GeoJSON 'date': '2026-10-13'; ArcGIS MapDate 2026-10-13), but the ArcGIS layer page's 'Last Edit Date' read 10/1/2026. Freshness must therefore come from the feature dates, not service metadata.
rules.limitations: Holidays can delay a release. Mirror services (IEM, ArcGIS) can lag the primary, which I did not measure.
rules.configurable: Threshold derives from the schedule. A small allowance for holidays could be configurable.
rules.missing_data_blocks: No valid date means the panel shows 'unavailable' with the last known valid date; it must not show a category.
rules.recommendation: Adopt alongside rule 1. Show the age in days next to the category.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Show the county USDM category mix and a count of weeks at D2 or worse in the last 8 weeks as information only, with a link to FSA. Do not compute or claim program eligibility.
rules.decision_supported: Awareness that drought designation may trigger FSA Livestock Forage Disaster Program paperwork, and drought-plan escalation
rules.required_inputs: Ranch county FIPS; weekly USDM % area by category for that county
rules.context: Ranches with grazed land in a USDM-rated county; LFP applies during the normal grazing period
rules.evidence: The FSA LFP page (fetched) says payments 'will now trigger after four consecutive weeks of qualifying severe drought'. It says 'D3 (Extreme Drought) at any time' qualifies for three monthly payments, and D4 for four weeks for five payments. It notes the thresholds changed and gives no effective date. The county service returns % of area in None/D0-D4 per week (observed for Hughes Co. SD).
rules.limitations: FSA rules change (the page itself says the old 8-week trigger is now 4 weeks). Eligibility is decided by FSA, not by a % area rule chosen in a dashboard. County % area does not say which part of the county the ranch is in.
rules.configurable: Yes. The rule for summarising a county (e.g., the worst category covering at least X% of area) is a ranch/dashboard choice, so X is C-class.
rules.missing_data_blocks: No county FIPS, or a gap in the weekly series, means no week count. Show 'incomplete series'.
rules.recommendation: Adopt as a context panel with no severity colour tied to eligibility. Link to FSA for the authoritative rules.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Show state-level NASS Crop Progress pasture and range condition (% very poor+poor and % good+excellent) with its week-ending date, as regional context only. No threshold triggers an exception.
rules.decision_supported: Whether the ranch's own forage picture is out of line with the state
rules.required_inputs: State; weekly NASS pasture & range condition; week-ending date; release time
rules.context: In-season weekly report. State level only; the KS 2026 and SD 2022 releases report one statewide figure.
rules.evidence: KS weekly, July 6 2026: 'Pasture and range conditions rated 5% very poor, 10% poor, 29% fair, 46% good, and 10% excellent'. SD weekly, Sept 12 2022: '24% very poor, 29% poor, 31% fair, 15% good, and 1% excellent'. Both say data were 'provided at the county level by USDA Farm Service Agency' and Extension reporters. NASS 2007: estimates 'are released after 4:00 pm ET on the first business day of the week'. NASS 2019 program review: 'Each state maintains a list of reporters, largely extension agents and Farm Service Agency staff'.
rules.limitations: Reporter judgement, state aggregate, seasonal. I did not verify the exact April-November window in this pass. The Quick Stats API needs a key (rnassqs vignette: 'the QuickStats API requires authentication'; 50,000-record limit), and the key would be exposed in browser JS.
rules.configurable: Any alert threshold would be a ranch choice (C); the display itself needs none.
rules.missing_data_blocks: Off-season or missing week: show 'no report for week ending X'. Do not carry the last value forward silently.
rules.recommendation: Optional, low priority. If used, fetch at build time with the key in a GitHub Actions secret.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Show the Grass-Cast seasonal grassland production outlook (% above or below the grid cell's ~38-year average) with its map date. Context only; never the sole basis for stocking.
rules.decision_supported: Early-season forage expectation feeding drought-plan trigger dates and stocking reviews
rules.required_inputs: Ranch location (grid cell or county); Grass-Cast map date and scenario; season window
rules.context: Great Plains rangeland, roughly late April to Aug 31. Grass-dominated cells are most accurate. Cropland, shrublands and forests are excluded.
rules.evidence: About page: 'Grass-Cast is updated every two weeks to incorporate newly observed weather data'; 10 km grid cells; 'Producers should not rely on Grass-Cast as a sole source for making management decisions'. Climate Hubs: first published typically late April; 'provides forecast information only for vegetation quantity, not quality'. Home page: 'As of August 31, 2026, all relevant precipitation data have been observed for the 2026 Grass-Cast season.' FAQ: 'most accurate in grid cells that are dominated by grass species'. Developer PDF: Grass-Cast 'knows Total Production Loss' not 'Grazing Loss' and reports 60-80% accuracy. That accuracy figure is the developers' own; no independent validation was found in this pass, and the 2021 user-report PDF was robots-blocked.
rules.limitations: Maps are images. Downloadable CSVs are historical averages (county and grid 1981-2018; annual grid 1982-2019), not the current forecast. No API. Cannot separate desirable from undesirable species. Does not account for local grazing history.
rules.configurable: Which scenario to show (above/near/below-normal precipitation) is a user choice.
rules.missing_data_blocks: Out of season: show the final map with 'season closed', or nothing. No location means no panel.
rules.recommendation: Optional. Snapshot the relevant season value manually or at build time with the map date. Do not scrape images in the browser.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Show RAP annual herbaceous production (lbs/acre) history per pasture polygon as retrospective context. Use it to sanity-check planned_graze_days, not to judge the current season.
rules.decision_supported: Whether a pasture's planned graze days are consistent with its production history; spotting long-run decline
rules.required_inputs: Pasture polygons (GeoJSON, EPSG:4326); RAP productionV3 results by year
rules.context: Rangeland only. RAP says production estimates 'are not to be used in agricultural lands, i.e., croplands'.
rules.evidence: RAP API doc: POST a GeoJSON Feature to 'https://us-central1-rap-data-365417.cloudfunctions.net/productionV3'; 'Valid years run from 1986 through the previous year'; results are a weighted mean over the pixels. Products page: 16-day current-year estimates 'are provisional and will be recalculated at the end of the year'. Production comes from a process-based model, so 'traditional error metrics such as RMSE are not available'. Cover MAE is 2.6% (tree) to 10.2% (perennial forb/grass). TOS (last updated Sept 11 2024): AS IS, no warranty.
rules.limitations: Through the API, the current year is not available. Model estimates; no ground truth on this ranch. The ranch is fictional, so it has no real polygons.
rules.missing_data_blocks: No polygons means no RAP. Do not substitute a county average for a pasture.
rules.recommendation: Defer. Worthwhile only with real pasture boundaries; for this fictional demo it would imply a real place. If used, fetch once offline and commit with provenance.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Cattle heat-stress outlook. From the NWS hourly forecast (temperature F, RH %, wind mph, cloud cover converted to solar W/m2), compute the USDA-ARS breathing-rate estimate BR = 2.83*T + 0.58*RH - 0.76*Wind + 0.039*Solar - 196.4 for T > 80 F. Categorise it Normal <90, Alert 90-110, Danger 110-130, Emergency >130 breaths/min. Warn when a planned gather or move falls on a Danger or worse day.
rules.decision_supported: Rescheduling cattle work and moves, and checking water, on hot days
rules.required_inputs: Location (lat/lon); NWS hourly forecast; planned work/move dates; cattle class
rules.context: Summer, mainly June to August in the Northern/Central Plains. Developed at USDA-ARS Clay Center NE; press coverage frames it for cattle feeders. For pasture cattle the evidence is weaker.
rules.evidence: The ARS 'Forecasting Heat Stress' page gives the equation and category table (Last Modified 8/12/2016). It suggests ~1000 W/m2 if no solar data and says the maps are 'an estimate of general trends' and 'cannot predict individual animal stress levels since there is much variability among animals'. The ARS index region page lists 7-day regional maps (Last Modified 7/26/2017); the forecast date is only in an image, which I could not read (forecastDate.png robots-blocked; curl to www.marc.ars.usda.gov returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'). Farm Progress (2020-07-08) and Drovers (2020-11-12) describe 7-day maps from NWS inputs. Drovers adds risk factors: 'high overnight lows (above 70 F)', low air movement, recent rain, and advises avoiding moving cattle during heat events.
rules.limitations: Whether the ARS maps are still published in 2026 is UNVERIFIED. Category boundaries at exactly 110 and 130 are ambiguous on the page. Cloud cover to solar conversion is an approximation. Night-time cooling and coat colour are not in the equation.
rules.configurable: Category cut-offs should stay as published. Which events trigger a warning (gathers, moves, shipping) is a ranch choice.
rules.missing_data_blocks: No forecast or no location means no heat panel. Do not show 'Normal' by default. Off-season (as_of Sept 30), suppress the panel instead of showing an empty one.
rules.recommendation: Optional and seasonal. Compute at build time from an NWS forecast snapshot; label it 'estimate of general trend, not individual animals'.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: In calving season, show a cold-stress outlook using the Comprehensive Climate Index (CCI). Use the newborn bands for calving pastures and the adult bands for others (e.g., Adult Cold Moderate -4 to 13 F; Newborn Cold Moderate 23 to 31 F). Raise it as a scheduling/observation prompt (check pairs, bedding, wind shelter), never as a treatment instruction.
rules.decision_supported: When to increase calving checks and plan shelter or feed logistics
rules.required_inputs: Hourly forecast temperature, RH, wind, solar/cloud; calving dates or expected calving window; location
rules.context: Winter/spring calving in ND, SD, NE
rules.evidence: NDAWN CCI page: CCI is 'calculated by adjusting the air temperature using relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation'. It 'does not take into account precipitation' and is 'not designed to predict apparent temperature for animals with wet hair coats'. 'Non-acclimated or sick animals should be evaluated using the Newborn CCI'. It gives a full band table and cites Mader, Johnson and Gaughan 2010 (J. Anim. Sci. 88:2153-2165). Per that abstract, the index was developed from 9 summer and 6 winter periods. KFYR (2026-02-19) reports NDAWN promoting it for cold-weather feeding and shelter decisions.
rules.limitations: The NDAWN map covers ND/MN (6 MT stations exist) and offers no download or API. SD/NE ranches would have to compute CCI themselves. Wet coats and precipitation are excluded, and calving losses depend on much more than weather.
rules.configurable: Bands should stay as published. Which band prompts extra checks is a ranch choice (C).
rules.missing_data_blocks: No calving window means no CCI prompt. No forecast means no panel.
rules.recommendation: Optional future feature tied to a calving calendar. Out of season at as_of 2026-09-30.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Rainfall against normal plus drought-plan trigger dates. Record the ranch rain gauge and compare 30/60/90-day totals with a public normal. At ranch-chosen calendar trigger dates, prompt the drought-plan review.
rules.decision_supported: Whether to start the drought contingency steps (destock, buy feed, defer pastures) on schedule
rules.required_inputs: Daily ranch gauge precip (in); public precip/normal (PRISM, IEM, ACIS); ranch trigger dates and actions
rules.context: Northern/Central Plains growing season; trigger dates are ranch-specific
rules.evidence: The NDMC 'Managing Drought Risk on the Ranch' plan page recommends 'Setting dates on the calendar when specific conditions warrant action'. It says monitoring 'helps you decide when it is time to act' and advises finding 'the earliest possible indicators of pending forage or water deficits'. It gives no numeric thresholds. Its Monitor page: 'If you suspect you may not produce enough forage to meet your herd's needs this year, it's time to take action', and it lists USDM, CoCoRaHS, VegDRI and Grass-Cast. PRISM web-service doc (26 Mar 2025): daily grids are updated 'eight times before becoming stable', and data older than six months are stable. So recent public precipitation values change after the fact.
rules.limitations: No threshold is evidence-backed in what I gathered; they are ranch choices. PRISM limits: a file downloaded twice in 24 h is blocked; commercial use prohibited without arrangement; zipped grids are not browser-friendly. I could not verify ACIS and NCEI CDO terms or token rules (ACIS docs page rendered empty; the CDO page did not state token or limits).
rules.configurable: Yes. Trigger dates, % of normal, and actions are all ranch-defined.
rules.missing_data_blocks: Gauge gaps longer than a few days should block a % of normal; show 'gauge record incomplete' and do not treat missing days as zero rain.
rules.recommendation: Adopt the ranch-gauge field and trigger-date checklist (cheap, credible). Treat public precip as optional build-time context with retrieved_at recorded.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Water days of supply = (level_pct x usable capacity_gal + expected refill over the period) / (head watering at the tank x intake gal/head/day by class and temperature). Warn below a ranch-set number of days. The current % thresholds (waterCritical 25, waterLow 40) ignore herd size and weather.
rules.decision_supported: Whether to haul water, fix supply, or move cattle before a tank runs dry
rules.required_inputs: tank capacity (gal), usable fraction, refill rate or haul schedule, head per tank (from moves/groups), class, forecast max temp, intake table
rules.context: Pasture tanks with float-fed or hauled supply; summer demand peaks
rules.evidence: NDSU AS1763 'Livestock Water Requirements' (revised Feb 2026; table from NRC 2016) gives gal/head/day by class and temperature. For example, Lactating 900 lb is 11.4 at 40 F, 16.9 at 70 F, 17.9 at 80 F, 16.2 at 90 F, and Growing 600 lb is 12.7 at 90 F. The page's extraction left the pregnant-cow columns unclear. Re-running context.research.mjs printed 'water.csv carries level_pct only, so gallons on hand = level_pct x capacity is NOT computable from repo data'. With an ASSUMED 10,000 gal tank it printed 'Cows @70F (lactating 900 lb row): 180 head x 16.9 = 3042 gal/day; tank 40% ... -> 1.31 days with zero refill'. NDMC Plan page: 'Upgrading or adding stock water tanks can improve grazing distribution and livestock health during drought.'
rules.limitations: Table values are estimates (the lactating row is not monotonic). Intake also varies with forage moisture and water quality (AS1764). Refill rate dominates for float-fed tanks. The 10,000 gal capacity is an assumption, not repo data.
rules.configurable: Yes. The alert threshold in days is C (ranch choice). Intake by class/temp is B, from a table. Current % thresholds are D (synthetic demo).
rules.missing_data_blocks: No capacity or refill data: show % only and state 'days of supply unavailable'. Never compute days from % alone.
rules.recommendation: Add capacity_gal and supply_type/refill_gph to a tanks table. Keep % thresholds labelled as demo settings until then.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Record a forage observation (residual height or utilization estimate, regrowth/recovery note, photo point) at move-out and before re-entry. Use it alongside min_rest_days, not replaced by satellite or forecast products.
rules.decision_supported: Whether a pasture is ready to graze again and whether planned graze days held
rules.required_inputs: obs_date, pasture_id, observer, residual/utilization, recovery_ready, photo id
rules.context: Rotational grazing on Northern/Central Plains rangeland
rules.evidence: Public products cannot replace field observation at pasture scale. Grass-Cast uses 10 km cells and 'cannot tell the difference between desirable forage species and undesirable species'. Its developers note total production differs from grazable production (worked example: take half, half trampled, about 25% usable). RAP gives no current-year data through its API. NDSU R1780 (Grazing Monitoring Stick) could not be fetched in this pass (CLIENT_ERROR), so I do not quote its recovery periods here.
rules.limitations: The method (stick height, utilization class, photo) is a ranch choice, and observer variation is real.
rules.missing_data_blocks: No observation within N days before a planned move-in: show 'recovery not checked', not 'ready'.
rules.recommendation: Adopt as a manual-observation CSV. It is the cheapest, most credible forage signal for a portfolio dashboard.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Feed and mineral inventory. Days on hand = quantity on hand / measured daily use. Warn when days on hand fall below the supplier lead time plus a buffer, and when the last count is stale.
rules.decision_supported: When to reorder hay, supplement or mineral; drought feed planning
rules.required_inputs: item, unit, on_hand, count_date, daily_use (measured from ranch records), lead_time_days
rules.context: Year-round; critical in drought and winter
rules.evidence: The NDMC Plan page recommends 'Adding flexibility to the operation's forage/feed resources' and an inventory of resources (Worksheet 3), but gives no inventory method. I found no extension intake rate for mineral in this pass: web search budget was exhausted. Consumption therefore has to come from the ranch's own records.
rules.limitations: Thin evidence gathered; no published thresholds used.
rules.missing_data_blocks: No count date or no use rate: show the quantity only, with no days on hand.
rules.recommendation: Optional. Low build cost; credible only if the use rate is measured, not assumed.

rules.rule: PROPOSED: Breeding and calving scheduling and records. Record breeding season start and end per group. Schedule pregnancy diagnosis no earlier than 35 days after bull removal for palpation (27 days for rectal ultrasound). Record pregnant/open for every exposed female. Prompt body condition scoring 60-90 days before calving, at calving and at weaning. Escalate to the herd veterinarian; give no treatment logic.
rules.decision_supported: Scheduling preg checks, BCS checks and calving-season staffing
rules.required_inputs: group, bull_in_date, bull_out_date, preg_check_date, method, result counts, BCS dates/scores
rules.context: Cow-calf and replacement heifers. The demo health.csv already has 'Heifers, Pregnancy check, next_due 2026-10-25'.
rules.evidence: BIF Pregnancy Data (last edited 27 Mar 2026): 'Pregnancy status (not pregnant or open vs. pregnant) should be recorded on each breeding female that was exposed to a bull'; palpation 'After 35 days post breeding'; rectal ultrasonography 'After 27 days post breeding'; methods 'should be conducted by trained personnel'. BIF Exposure Data (last edited 12 Apr 2021): 'producers should indicate breeding season start and end dates'. BIF Body Condition Scores (last edited 2 Jun 2022): 'scores should be recorded 60-90 days pre-calving, at calving and at weaning'.
rules.limitations: BIF guidelines are written for genetic-evaluation recording, so the timing is a minimum, not an optimum. Expected calving window needs a gestation length I did not source in this pass; label it as an assumption.
rules.configurable: Lead times and who performs checks: yes (ranch and veterinarian).
rules.missing_data_blocks: No bull_out_date: the earliest valid preg-check date cannot be computed, so show 'breeding dates missing'.
rules.recommendation: Adopt as scheduling fields; it extends the existing health task list without any diagnosis.

feature_notes:
ARCHITECTURE (recommended for a static GitHub Pages site with no backend): do not fetch public data from the browser at view time. Add a separate, manually triggered or scheduled GitHub Actions workflow ('refresh-context') that fetches a small set of sources for a labelled stand-in county around the fictional as_of. It writes data/context.csv with value, unit, area, valid_date, released_at, retrieved_at, source_url and attribution. The test workflow stays offline and deterministic. This avoids four problems at once: CORS is unverified for every endpoint; NASS needs a key, which would be public in browser JS; api.weather.gov wants a User-Agent, which browsers may not let a page set (unverified); and live data would not match the fictional as_of (observed: live USDM valid 2026-10-13 versus ranch as_of 2026-09-30). Credible, low-maintenance picks: (1) USDM county statistics (free, no key, weekly, NDMC attribution); (2) optionally Grass-Cast season outlook and NASS state pasture condition as manual or build-time snapshots; (3) NWS forecast-derived heat (ARS breathing-rate) or cold (CCI) panels only if seasonal. Exclude: SD Mesonet (redistribution banned); Nebraska Mesonet (no data access page yet); NDAWN ingestion (no API; terms unverified); RAP and NRCS soils (need real polygons); PRISM in the browser (zipped grids, download caps); HeatRisk (human index); the ARS heat maps as a dependency (2026 status unverified).

OBSERVED in this audit: (a) USDM row selection. node docs/audit/diagnostics/context.usdm-asof.research.mjs shows the naive validity-window lookup picks MapDate 20260929 (D0 31.55%), which was released 2026-10-01 08:30 ET, after as_of. The release-aware lookup picks 20260922 (D0 8.27%). (b) The existing context.research.mjs, re-run, reports no location, time zone, tank capacity, rain gauge, forage observation, inventory or maintenance fields in data/*.csv. It also reports a USDM valid-date age of 8.5 days at as_of, and NASS week ending 2026-09-27 released 2026-09-28 16:00 ET. (c) The ArcGIS USDM layer's epoch times convert to 07:30 UTC, and its 'Last Edit Date' (10/1/2026) lags the features (2026-10-13). (d) The USDM cutoff wording differs across official pages (8 a.m. EDT vs 7 a.m. ET/EST).

CANDIDATE FEATURES (brief evidence):
- Pasture recovery and forage observations: best value for credibility. Public products are coarse or model-based. Grass-Cast uses 10 km cells, cannot tell desirable from undesirable species, and estimates total, not grazable, production. RAP's API stops at the previous year. So a manual forage observation at move-out and before move-in (class C) is the honest signal.
- Rainfall, drought and heat context: USDM weekly county context (A/B), ranch rain gauge (C), and drought-plan trigger dates (NDMC says to set calendar dates; no thresholds published, class C). Heat: ARS breathing-rate categories (B; general trend, not individual animals). Cold: CCI newborn/adult bands (B; excludes wet coats and precipitation).
- Water storage and days of supply: needs tank capacity and refill data that the repo lacks. Intake by class and temperature comes from NDSU AS1763 (rev. Feb 2026; NRC 2016 table). The current 25%/40% thresholds are demo settings (D). The days-of-supply alert threshold is a ranch choice (C).
- Fence and equipment maintenance logs; crew task tracking: no published intervals gathered (search budget exhausted). Class C. One sourced interval: NDSU's weekly waterer disinfection (2-3 oz of 5.25% bleach per 50 gal).
- Calving and breeding tasks: BIF guidelines support recording breeding season start/end, pregnancy status for every exposed female, and diagnosis timing (palpation after 35 days, ultrasound after 27 days), plus BCS 60-90 days pre-calving, at calving and at weaning. Scheduling and records only; escalate to the veterinarian.
- Feed and mineral inventory: the NDMC drought plan supports feed flexibility and a resource inventory, but no intake rates were sourced. Days on hand must use measured ranch consumption (C).

FILES CREATED (new, under the allowed diagnostics folder; no existing file modified, nothing committed):
- /home/claude/ranch-ops-dashboard/docs/audit/diagnostics/context.usdm-asof.research.mjs (offline; demonstrates release-aware vs naive USDM selection)
- /home/claude/ranch-ops-dashboard/docs/audit/diagnostics/context.cors.research.mjs (network CORS probe for 10 endpoints, to run where internet is open; in the sandbox every probe failed with ENOTFOUND, or through the proxy with a 403 on CONNECT)
Scratch dir created: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude-ranch-ops-dashboard/c61c6ab5-2745-59d3-9dda-44a2053cd423/scratchpad/audit/research-context/ (empty).
caveats:
1) The web search budget (shared across agents) ran out after about 25 searches. Unresearched as a result: extension sources for mineral and feed intake, maintenance intervals, crew-task evidence, gestation length, NWS API CORS behaviour, NASS's exact in-season window, and ACIS/NCEI terms. A follow-up message can resume the search.
2) No CORS header was observed for any source. curl to api.weather.gov, usdmdataservices.unl.edu, quickstats.nass.usda.gov, climate.sdstate.edu, ndawn.ndsu.nodak.edu and www.marc.ars.usda.gov returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. Node fetch returned ENOTFOUND without the proxy and failed with it. All browser-side claims are therefore UNVERIFIED; run docs/audit/diagnostics/context.cors.research.mjs elsewhere.
3) Failed or blocked fetches: api.weather.gov (robots), quickstats.nass.usda.gov/api (robots), ndawn.ndsu.nodak.edu (robots), droughtmonitor.unl.edu/CurrentMap.aspx (robots), marc.ars.usda.gov forecastDate.png (robots), ARS heat-stress docs/main page (client error), usda.gov Grass-Cast blog (client error), NDSU R1780 grazing stick (client error), the IEM prism.py help (client error), and the Grass-Cast 2021 user-report PDF (robots). The ACIS docs page rendered no content.
4) Whether the USDA-ARS cattle heat stress forecast is still published in 2026 is UNVERIFIED: pages last modified 2016 and 2017, and the date appears only in an image.
5) Vendor or developer claims are separated from independent evidence. The Grass-Cast 60-80% accuracy figure comes from the developers. RAP accuracy (cover MAE 2.6-10.2%) comes from RAP's own product page. No independent validation of either was gathered.
6) WebFetch returns model-summarised page text. Quotes come from those summaries, and table cells, such as the NDSU pregnant-cow columns, may be misaligned; check the originals before reusing numbers.
7) No threshold here is universally validated. Category cut-offs (ARS breathing rate, CCI bands, USDM D-categories) are published definitions. Alert thresholds layered on them are ranch choices, and the dashboard's current water/grazing/gain/budget thresholds are demo settings.
8) FSA LFP rules are quoted from an undated page that says they recently changed; eligibility must not be inferred by the dashboard.
9) Hughes County, SD was used only as an example real county for API checks; the dashboard ranch is fictional and has no location.
10) The working tree's HEAD is bff0ba9 (audit WIP commits on top of cfd77e5), not cfd77e5 itself. Existing file docs/audit/diagnostics/context.research.mjs, from an earlier run, was read and re-run but not modified.
